focus: deepseek-02: The cli-deem lifecycle: install, start, health, update and rollback

label: deem-ctl is a complete 208-line lifecycle: start/stop/status/update(--check) with exit taxonomy 0-4; all state under DEEM_HOME; keep live+previous model
deem-ctl health refuses stub (backend torch or ensemble: without stub), retries 120x1s, smoke = one real choice; it does not pin the model id
Start pins DEEM_MODEL_ID=deem-0.8-v1, DEEM_DEVICE=mps, 127.0.0.1:8300, HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1; a start never downloads
Update: revision check via HF/GitHub APIs, partial download+rename, fetch, stop, symlink+checkout, restart+smoke, rollback exit 3, prune to live+previous, exit 2 on check/download failure
Rollback built into update; removal is rm -rf ~/.local/share/deem; un-journalled window between stop and switch; next update repairs both shas
start and a stopped-server update never prove a real decision; a checkpoint that loads but cannot decide would be served silently
Repo embedder supervision has respawn lock, crash-loop backoff, opt-in idle eviction, drain, RSS watchdog; Deem needs none repo-side but has no idle eviction (3,368 MB held idle)
stop_server does not wait for exit and wait_healthy proves a healthy port, not the new PID; inferred small race, one-line wait-for-exit hardening
No served commit in /health; commit pair lives in deem-ctl status (model sha from symlink, source sha from git); every Deem measurement must record the pair
Served instance binds loopback (vendor example binds 0.0.0.0); CORS * and no auth means any local process/page can call; operator + launchd own start/stop; no repo-side spawn allowed
Update download excludes v1.0/* and prune keeps two checkpoints, bounding disk at two model dirs plus venv; rollback target always retained
